name: Non-syndromic Hemimelia

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and Radiological Diagnostic Criteria for Hemimelia

criteria.description: Congenital partial or complete absence of one or more long bones in a limb without associated syndromic features
No presence of systemic or syndromic anomalies such as craniofacial, cardiac, or neurological abnormalities
Radiological evidence confirming the absence or hypoplasia of specific limb bones consistent with hemimelia
Negative or non-contributory family history of syndromic limb defects

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of congenital limb bone absence or hypoplasia without syndromic features confirmed by radiographic imaging
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis relies primarily on clinical and imaging findings; genetic testing may be performed to exclude syndromic causes.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Congenital absence of distal long bones in a limb
searchTerms: absence of lower arm or leg bones
no distal long bones in limb

pathognomonic.symptomName: Unilateral limb length discrepancy due to bone deficiency
searchTerms: one limb shorter due to missing bone
unequal limb length from bone loss
shorter arm or leg on one side

common.symptomName: Limited range of motion in affected limb joints
searchTerms: stiff joints in affected arm or leg

common.symptomName: Muscle hypoplasia or atrophy in affected limb
searchTerms: small or weak muscles in affected limb
muscle underdevelopment in arm or leg

common.symptomName: Gait abnormalities secondary to limb length discrepancy
searchTerms: walking problems from uneven limb length
limp due to leg length difference
abnormal gait from limb size difference

occasional.symptomName: Compensatory scoliosis due to limb length discrepancy
searchTerms: spine curvature from leg length difference
uneven spine due to limb length
scoliosis caused by leg length mismatch

occasional.symptomName: Mild limb deformities such as clubfoot
Skin dimpling or scarring over affected limb segments
searchTerms: skin dimples or scars on limb

occasional.symptomName: Secondary joint contractures in affected limb

rare.symptomName: Neuropathic changes due to altered limb innervation
searchTerms: altered limb sensation from nerve issues
vascular malformations in arm or leg

rare.symptomName: Mild limb edema due to lymphatic disruption
searchTerms: mild swelling in limb from lymph issues
limb edema due to lymphatic problems

imaging: Radiographs showing absence or hypoplasia of long bones in affected limb
MRI or CT may be used to assess soft tissue and bone anatomy
genetic: Typically no known pathogenic variants identified in isolated cases
Genetic testing performed to exclude syndromic limb reduction defects
other: Clinical examination revealing unilateral limb shortening and deformity
Absence of systemic anomalies differentiates from syndromic forms

distinguishingFeatures: Multiple congenital anomalies including vertebral, anal, cardiac, tracheoesophageal, renal, and limb defects
Presence of syndromic features beyond limb reduction

redFlags: Presence of systemic anomalies suggesting syndromic diagnosis
Rapid progression of limb deformity or vascular compromise
Signs of infection or ischemia in affected limb
references: Hunter AGW, et al. Limb Reduction Defects. In: Emery’s Elements of Medical Genetics. 14th ed. 2013.
